title: add backfill & manifesting tooling + TTL enforcement for private S3 audit sinks
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Private installs in regulated regions often onboard long-running S3 sinks created before the audit-exporter reconciler existed. We saw multiple incidents where old sinks had no lifecycle/TTL or inconsistent manifesting, causing retention policy gaps and failed replays. This PR introduces an idempotent backfill job that generates 'sink-manifest' objects for existing private S3 buckets, plus a conservative TTL enforcement policy and Helm hooks to wire the job into Private installs. Motivation: ensure compliance (jurisdictional retention and guaranteed export manifests) during upgrades and migrations without forcing immediate manual work for customers. What this PR does: 1) backfill job: a Kubernetes CronJob + a one-shot Job mode that discovers buckets referenced by cluster config and creates SinkManifest CRs with source metadata and inferred retention. The job is fully idempotent and rate-limited to avoid S3 throttling. 2) manifest CRD: lightweight SinkManifest CRD + controller to reconcile manifests into the existing export pipeline (audit log exporter -> tombstone/manifesting stage). 3) TTL enforcement: adds a TTL controller that adds S3 lifecycle hints and emits audit events when retention < minimum for region/compliance tier. This is configurable via helm values and guarded by a feature flag 'backfill.enable'. 4) Helm: chart changes add pre-upgrade and post-upgrade hooks to run the one-shot backfill during upgrades and to roll back in case of failure. 5) Terraform: module updates to add IAM role bindings for the backfill job in Private installer docs; also a migration helper to grant read/list permissions only during backfill window. 6) tests and e2e: unit tests for controller logic, integration test that runs the job against a local-minio fixture, and a smoke test that validates manifests are created and reconciled. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout across Private installs; default disabled for air-gapped customers. Backwards compatibility: controller no-ops if SinkManifest CRD already exists and handles duplicate buckets gracefully. Checklist: - [x] CRD and controller - [x] Backfill job (CronJob + one-shot) - [x] Helm hooks and values - [x] Terraform IAM docs + migration helper - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Migration README + runbook for SRE - [x] Feature flag gating - [x] Observability: metrics for backfilled count, failures, S3 errors Migration notes: operators should run the one-shot in read-only mode to preview manifests (helm value backfill.preview=true) then flip to backfill.preview=false to create manifests. For very large tenants we provide a chunked mode (backfill.chunkSize) and backoff settings. Security notes: backfill job uses short-lived credentials and requires explicit consent via terraform migration helper. This description is intentionally long to capture the compliance and operational requirements for Private deployments.

Maya Chen: added chunkSize + rateLimit config (defaults conservative). Integration tests cover chunking edge cases.

release_notes: Added idempotent backfill tooling to generate SinkManifest CRs for existing S3 buckets in Private installs; Helm hooks to run backfill during upgrades; TTL enforcement controller and Terraform migration helper for IAM; feature-flagged and disabled by default for air-gapped customers.
